sources.title: GPT-3.5 Turbo model documentation
sources.evidence: The complete current Markdown identifies model ID gpt-3.5-turbo, default snapshot gpt-3.5-turbo-0125, 16,385-token context and text input/output. It explicitly states that API access ended October 23, 2026. The HTML feature table says function calling is unsupported, conflicting with explicit earlier capability announcements; no explanation for that discrepancy is supplied.

sources.title: Introducing ChatGPT and Whisper APIs
sources.evidence: The launch names gpt-3.5-turbo and explains that the unpinned name follows a recommended model while dated snapshots can be selected. Its current displayed date is an April 24, 2024 editorial update, not the original launch date. It documents text messages and code/natural-language tasks.

sources.title: OpenAI API launch announcement, March 1, 2023
sources.evidence: The dated opening announcement by OpenAI developer-relations staff member Logan Kilpatrick states that the ChatGPT and Whisper APIs are now available and links the original launch article. Used only for first-party release timing; replies from other users are not technical evidence.

sources.title: Function calling and other API updates
sources.evidence: June 13, 2023 announcement explicitly adds trained function calling to gpt-3.5-turbo-0613, describes JSON function arguments, and schedules the generic alias upgrade on June 27. It distinguishes the original 0301 snapshot and the then-separate 16K model.

sources.title: New embedding models and API updates
sources.evidence: January 25, 2024 announcement identifies 0125, a fix for non-English function-call encoding, and migration of the generic gpt-3.5-turbo alias from 0613 to 0125. This supports function calling for the alias target; it does not make 0125 the March 2023 launch checkpoint.

sources.title: OpenAI model deprecations
sources.evidence: The April 22, 2026 legacy-model notice records October 23, 2026 shutdown for 0125 and the gpt-3.5-turbo alias. This is service status rather than a change to the model release date or historical capabilities.

sources.title: GPT-4 Technical Report
sources.evidence: The report compares GPT-3.5 Turbo in factuality and safety figures and distinguishes multiple ChatGPT revisions. The reviewed comparisons disclose no Turbo parameter count, active count, or exact dense-versus-expert architecture. Benchmark reasoning performance does not define a dedicated reasoning mode.

sources.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization
sources.evidence: The training study explicitly excludes GPT-2, GPT-3 and GPT-3.5 from its GPT-4-family experimental series. GPT-3.5-level performance labels therefore do not disclose the commercial Turbo model architecture or size.

sources.title: Introducing gpt-oss
sources.evidence: The August 2025 release states these were OpenAI’s first open-weight language models since GPT-2. This corroborates the hosted GPT-3.5 Turbo family was not an open-weight release; gpt-oss counts are not transferred to Turbo.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: The current agreement applies to OpenAI APIs, reserves service IP rights and provides limited service access. It supports a descriptive proprietary classification, not a named downloadable-checkpoint license or a claim that these exact 2026 terms applied at the 2023 launch.

name.note: Use the official display name; the identifier remains the unpinned gpt-3.5-turbo alias.

developer.note: Official model documentation and launch identify OpenAI.

family.note: Use the specific GPT-3.5 family rather than generic GPT.

release_date.note: Original public API launch date for the alias. Later alias-target upgrades and shutdown are separate events.

open_weights.note: Hosted proprietary release; first-party open-weight release history confirms this family was not distributed as open weights.

license.note: Descriptive classification of the closed hosted model. No open checkpoint license is asserted.

parameters_b.note: No total is disclosed for this alias or its 0125 target in the inspected model documentation, launch/update material or later first-party comparison/training reports. Do not transfer GPT-3’s 175B count or infer an exact architecture from the family name.

active_parameters_b.note: No active-per-token count is reported in the inspected exact-model documentation or first-party research. No total or sibling count is substituted.

architecture.note: Targeted first-party architecture, training and interpretability searches did not verify a dense or expert-routed design for this exact alias target. Later research comparison labels do not establish production architecture. Keep null.

context_window.note: Exact last-documented context for the alias’s 0125 target, not the original March 2023 snapshot. The service is now shut down; this does not assert current endpoint availability.

modalities.note: The model documentation specifies text input/output; code is text, not a separate modality.

reasoning.note: Clear the unsupported false assertion. Reviewed sources do not explicitly define support or non-support for a dedicated reasoning mode; general reasoning benchmarks do not resolve this flag.

tool_call.note: Historical model capability is explicitly documented: 0613 introduced trained function calling, the alias upgraded, and 0125 fixed function-call encoding. The current HTML feature table conflicts by saying unsupported; retain the explicit release evidence and record the conflict rather than erase historical support. This is not a claim that the shut-down API works today or that 0301 had the feature.

description.value: Chat model for text and code tasks, with an unpinned alias that last pointed to gpt-3.5-turbo-0125.

New embedding models and API updates

patch.notes: The alias launched March 1, 2023 and last pointed to gpt-3.5-turbo-0125; its 16,385-token context describes that later target, not the original 0301 snapshot. Function calling is documented by the June 2023 upgrade and January 2024 release, despite a conflicting current model-page feature table. OpenAI shut down API access on October 23, 2026. Parameter counts and exact architecture remain undisclosed or unverified.

summary: Verified original alias release and its later 0125 mapping, 16,385-token context, text modalities and proprietary closed access. Corrected tool calling to its explicitly documented historical support, with the current-table conflict and October 2026 shutdown recorded. Cleared unsupported reasoning=false; no speculative counts or architecture were introduced.
